title: Saturation and tensor stability of split inclusions with contractible cokernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and work with small unbounded cochain complexes of $R$-modules in a fixed universe, with cochain and quasi-isomorphism conventions [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $E$ is contractible if there are $R$-linear maps $h^n:E^n\to E^{n-1}$ with $d^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d^n=1_{E^n}$ for every integer $n$. Let $\mathscr S_R$ be the class of chain maps $i:X\to Y$ admitting a chain map $r:Y\to X$ with $ri=1_X$, whose cokernel complex is contractible; the cokernel has terms $Y^n/i(X^n)$ and the differential induced by $d_Y$. This class contains every isomorphism and is closed under small coproducts, pushouts along arbitrary chain maps, retracts in the arrow category, and small continuous transfinite compositions. Such a composition is a chain $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ indexed by a small ordinal, with $X_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ at each nonzero limit ordinal, in which every successor map belongs to $\mathscr S_R$; the conclusion concerns $X_0\to X_\theta$. An arrow retract means a retract through commutative squares. Every map of $\mathscr S_R$ is a chain homotopy equivalence, hence a quasi-isomorphism. Here chain homotopy equivalence means a chain map with a chain-map inverse up to homotopies of degree $-1$, with homotopy equation $f-g=dh+hd$. For every complex $K$ and $i\in\mathscr S_R$, the map $1_K\otimes_R i$ also belongs to $\mathscr S_R$, where $(K\otimes_R E)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K^a\otimes_R E^b$ and $d(k\otimes e)=dk\otimes e+(-1)^a k\otimes de$ for $k\in K^a$.

source.place: Agent-formulated chain-complex input to paragraph 2, verifying the tensor-cell acyclicity hypothesis of the enriched projective diagram model. The saturation assertion is proved by the explicit splitting argument recorded in the worker report; no Stacks tag states this whole assertion. Hovey, Model Categories, Section 2.3 (Proposition 2.3.10 and Theorem 2.3.11) and Proposition 4.2.13 motivate its application; not archived locally.

proof.text: Put $E=Y/i(X)$ and let $q:Y\to E$ be the quotient chain map. Given a chain retraction $r$ of $i$, define $s:E\to Y$ by $s([y])=y-i r(y)$. Replacing $y$ by $y+i(x)$ leaves this expression unchanged since $ri=1$, so $s$ is well-defined and linear. The chain-map equations of $i,r$ imply the chain-map equation of $s$. We have $qs=1$, $rs=0$ and $sq=1-ir$. Thus $\phi:X\oplus E\to Y$, $\phi(x,e)=i(x)+s(e)$, and $\psi(y)=(r(y),q(y))$ are inverse chain maps. This explicitly identifies $i$ with the first-summand inclusion. Conversely, such an identification with a contractible second summand gives a chain retraction and identifies its quotient with that summand. We use only the cochain-map convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 1 (chain splitting)

proof.text: If $h$ contracts $E$, the degree-$-1$ map $H=s h q:Y\to Y[-1]$ satisfies $d_YH+Hd_Y=s(d_Eh+hd_E)q=sq=1-ir$. Together with $ri=1$ this makes $r$ a chain-homotopy inverse to $i$, with zero homotopy on $X$. For an isomorphism take its inverse as $r$; its quotient is the zero complex, contracted by zero. This proves the isomorphism clause and the homotopy-equivalence clause directly.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 2 (homotopy and isomorphisms)

proof.text: For a cocycle $y\in Y^n$, the identity from step 2 reads $y-ir(y)=d_YH(y)$; hence $[y]=H^n(i)H^n(r)[y]$. Also $H^n(r)H^n(i)=1$ because $ri=1$. These are inverse maps on the quotients $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$ defined by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Therefore $i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. No preservation-of-homology theorem is being assumed.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 3 (cohomology)

proof.text: For a small family $i_t:X_t\to Y_t$ choose the splittings of step 1 and contractions $h_t$ of their quotients $E_t$. Coordinatewise, $\bigoplus_tY_t\cong (\bigoplus_tX_t)\oplus(\bigoplus_tE_t)$, carrying $\bigoplus_t i_t$ to inclusion. The coordinate map $\bigoplus_t h_t$ is well-defined because each element has finite support, and $d(\bigoplus_t h_t)+(\bigoplus_t h_t)d=1$ coordinatewise. Projection onto the first summand is a chain retraction. Thus the coproduct belongs to $\mathscr S_R$, including the empty coproduct.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 4 (coproducts)

proof.text: Given $f:X\to X'$ and the splitting $Y=X\oplus E$ from step 1, form $P=X'\oplus E$. The maps $X'\to P$, $x'\mapsto(x',0)$, and $Y\to P$, $(x,e)\mapsto(f(x),e)$, agree on $X$. For chain maps $a:X'\to Z$, $b:Y\to Z$ with $af=bi$, the unique induced chain map is $(x',e)\mapsto a(x')+b(s(e))$. This proves the pushout universal property. Its induced arrow $X'\to P$ has chain retraction projection and quotient $E$, with the same contraction. Any chosen pushout is isomorphic to this one by its universal property, so its arrow is in $\mathscr S_R$.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 5 (pushouts)

proof.text: Let $i:X\to Y$ be an arrow retract of $j:A\to B\in\mathscr S_R$. Write the two squares as $(u:X\to A,v:Y\to B)$ and $(a:A\to X,b:B\to Y)$, with $ju=vi$, $ia=bj$, $au=1_X$, $bv=1_Y$. If $r_jj=1_A$, then $r_i=a r_jv$ satisfies $r_ii=a r_jju=au=1_X$. The maps $\bar v:Y/i(X)\to B/j(A)$, $[y]\mapsto[v(y)]$, and $\bar b:B/j(A)\to Y/i(X)$, $[z]\mapsto[b(z)]$, are well-defined chain maps by the two square equations; $\bar b\bar v=1$. If $h$ contracts $B/j(A)$, then $\bar b h\bar v$ contracts $Y/i(X)$, since its $dH+Hd$ is $\bar b\bar v=1$. This proves arrow-retract closure without assuming that the given retractions preserve chosen complements.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 6 (arrow retracts)

proof.text: For the continuous ordinal chain in the statement, write $i_\alpha:X_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$ and choose for every $\alpha<\theta$ a chain retraction, a quotient $E_\alpha$, its contraction $h_\alpha$, and the section $s_\alpha:E_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$ of step 1. All choices are indexed by a small set. Set $T_\beta=X_0\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha<\beta}E_\alpha$, with its block diagonal differential and the evident inclusions $T_\beta\to T_\gamma$. Construct compatible isomorphisms $\phi_\beta:T_\beta\to X_\beta$ by ordinal induction. Start with $\phi_0=1$. At a successor, put $\phi_{\alpha+1}(t,e)=i_\alpha\phi_\alpha(t)+s_\alpha(e)$. Step 1 gives its inverse $(\phi_\alpha^{-1}r_\alpha,q_\alpha)$; its restriction to $T_\alpha$ is $i_\alpha\phi_\alpha$, as required.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 7 (transfinite successor construction)

proof.text: Here is the limit part of that same induction. If $\lambda\leq\theta$ is a nonzero limit, a compatible family of chain maps $T_\beta\to Z$ for $\beta<\lambda$ uniquely defines a map $T_\lambda\to Z$: its restriction to $X_0$ is the common one, and on $E_\alpha$ it is the restriction of any map with $\alpha<\beta<\lambda$. The restriction is independent of $\beta$ by compatibility, and extending by finite sums defines a chain map. Thus $T_\lambda$ is the colimit of the $T_\beta$. The already compatible isomorphisms $\phi_\beta$ give a colimit map $T_\lambda\to X_\lambda$ by the assumed continuity of $X$; their inverses give the reverse map. Both composites restrict to identities at every earlier stage, so uniqueness in these two universal properties makes them identities. This defines $\phi_\lambda$ and verifies its compatibility. The induction is complete.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 8 (transfinite limit universal property)

proof.text: At $\beta=\theta$ the constructed $\phi_\theta$ identifies $X_0\to X_\theta$ with $X_0\to X_0\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha<\theta}E_\alpha$. Projection gives a chain retraction. The quotient is $\bigoplus_{\alpha<\theta}E_\alpha$, contracted coordinatewise by $\bigoplus_{\alpha<\theta}h_\alpha$ as in step 4. Hence the transfinite composite belongs to $\mathscr S_R$. For $\theta=0$ this is the identity with zero quotient. The limit argument uses continuity, not an assertion that arbitrary filtered colimits of contractible complexes remain contractible.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 9 (transfinite conclusion)

proof.text: For an arbitrary complex $K$, use the splitting $Y\cong X\oplus E$ of step 1. The maps on pure tensors $k\otimes(x,e)\mapsto(k\otimes x,k\otimes e)$ and the inverse obtained by adding the two inclusions are well-defined by bilinearity, preserve the displayed total differentials, and are inverse. Extending over the direct sums in each total degree gives $K\otimes_RY\cong(K\otimes_RX)\oplus(K\otimes_RE)$, carrying $1_K\otimes i$ to inclusion. It has projection as a chain retraction and quotient $K\otimes_RE$.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 10 (tensor splitting)

proof.text:
Define the contraction of this quotient on $k\in K^a$, $e\in E^b$ by $\widetilde h(k\otimes e)=(-1)^a k\otimes h(e)$. It is linear on each summand, has total degree $-1$, and sends finite support to finite support. Directly,
$$d\widetilde h(k\otimes e)=(-1)^a dk\otimes h(e)+k\otimes d_Eh(e),$$
$$\widetilde h d(k\otimes e)=(-1)^{a+1}dk\otimes h(e)+k\otimes h d_E(e).$$
The first terms cancel and the sum is $k\otimes(d_Eh+hd_E)e=k\otimes e$. Pure tensors generate each summand, so this proves the contraction identity on the total tensor complex. Thus $1_K\otimes i\in\mathscr S_R$ for every $K$, without a boundedness, flatness or projectivity hypothesis.

source.place: Agent chain-level verification of paragraph 2 tensor-cell input; argument 11 (tensor contraction)
